name: Investment due diligence
instructions:
You write a first-pass due diligence memo on ONE private company for an investment team.

Sections (each a list of short claims, every claim with a source_url and a date):
- business: what it sells, to whom, business model, geographies.
- traction: named customers, customer counts, growth statements, partnerships. Mark company claims as "company claim".
- team: founders and current executives, prior companies, notable departures in the last 2 years.
- funding: rounds, dates, amounts, lead investors, last known valuation.
- financial_signals: revenue statements or estimates (labelled with who estimated), headcount trend, hiring or layoffs.
- legal_and_regulatory: lawsuits, regulatory actions, data breaches, sanctions exposure. Court dockets and regulator sites
  first.
- reputation: employee reviews trend, customer complaint patterns, critical press.
- red_flags: only items backed by a cited claim above.
- verdict: 2-3 sentences: what looks strong, what needs a closer look.

Prefer filings, registries, court records, the company's own pages and reputable press. Label aggregator data.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.

missing_fields.description: fields you could not verify from a page you opened

inputs: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling
Write a due diligence memo on Canva
Write a due diligence memo on Deel
Write a due diligence memo on Databricks
Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

unit.name: material finding
unit.definition: One unit per distinct material finding a deal team would use: each funding round, valuation, revenue/traction figure, named customer, executive, lawsuit or regulatory action, red flag, etc. Descriptive filler and restatements are not units.
unit.verify_rule: true if the finding is correct and attributable to this company; dated claims must have the right date.

scoring_rule: Unit = material finding, weighted for an investment committee deciding today: critical 6, useful 2, minor 0.5; x1.5 when fresh. Red-flag recall reported separately.

name: Credit and counterparty risk assessment
instructions:
You assess whether ONE company can pay its debts and honour its obligations.

Collect, each item with a date and source_url:
- financials: latest revenue, operating income or EBITDA, cash, total debt, and any stated liquidity (revolver,
  cash runway). Public companies: the latest 10-K/10-Q or annual report. Private: filed accounts (UK Companies House,
  EU registries) or statements from the company or press; label who stated it.
- credit_ratings: current ratings and outlook from S&P, Moody's, Fitch or others, and any change in the last 12 months.
- debt_events: new financings, refinancings, covenant amendments or breaches, missed payments, defaults, distressed
  exchanges, bankruptcy filings.
- payment_behaviour: supplier complaints, liens, judgments, collection suits, late-payment reports.
- ownership: owner type (public, PE-backed by X, founder) and any recent change of control or sponsor.
- distress_signals: layoffs, hiring freezes, plant or office closures, executive departures (esp. CFO), auditor
  changes or going-concern language, large customer losses.
- risk_call: low / moderate / elevated / high, with 2-3 sentences that cite the items above.
Prefer filings, rating-agency releases, court records and reputable press. Do not use a parent's figures for a subsidiary.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.

missing_fields.description: fields you could not verify from a page you opened

Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Carvana
Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Beyond Meat
Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Wolfspeed
Assess the credit and counterparty risk of AMC Entertainment

unit.name: credit fact
unit.definition: One unit per distinct credit-relevant fact: each financial figure (metric+period), each rating action, each debt event, each payment-behaviour item, each distress signal, ownership. Restatements are not units.
unit.verify_rule: true if the fact is correct for this exact entity and period.

scoring_rule: Unit = credit fact, weighted for a lender deciding today: critical 6 (current defaults, ratings, liquidity, leverage, active proceedings), useful 2, minor 0.5; x1.5 when fresh.

name: KYC, AML and compliance screening
instructions:
You run a KYC screen on ONE company in the country given.

1. registration: legal name, registry number, LEI, jurisdiction, incorporation date, registered address and status,
   read from the national registry and GLEIF. If the operating name maps to several entities, pick the main operating
   company and list the others in related_entities. A branch is not the entity.
2. people: current directors/officers and persons with significant control or beneficial owners (e.g. Companies House
   PSC register), with role, nationality if stated, and source.
3. sanctions: check the entity and its owners against OFAC SDN, UK OFSI and EU consolidated lists. Report matches with
   the list name and why it is (or is not) the same party.
4. pep: flag owners or directors who are politically exposed persons, with evidence.
5. adverse_media: enforcement actions, fines, fraud, money-laundering or corruption allegations, sanctions evasion,
   lawsuits in the last 10 years, each with date, severity (high / medium / low), status and source.
6. risk_rating: low / medium / high with a one-paragraph rationale citing the items above.
Drop findings you cannot tie to this entity and count them in namesakes_excluded.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.
inputs: Run a KYC screen on Revolut in the United Kingdom
Run a KYC screen on Wirecard in Germany
Run a KYC screen on Greensill Capital in the United Kingdom
Run a KYC screen on Binance in France
Run a KYC screen on Adyen in the Netherlands

unit.name: KYC fact
unit.definition: One unit per registration field (legal name, registry number, LEI, jurisdiction, incorporation date, registered address, status), per officer/owner (name+role), and per sanctions, PEP or adverse-media finding.
unit.verify_rule: true if correct for this exact legal entity (not a parent, branch or namesake); findings must really concern this entity.

judge_tag.spec: "group": "registration|people|screening", "field": short field name; for screening units also "materiality": "critical|useful|minor" (for a compliance officer deciding today) and "false_hit": true|false (true ONLY if the finding is about the wrong entity or the event did not happen at all; a wrong date, figure or wording on a real finding is false_hit false); for every unit also "related_entity": true|false (true when it is about a group entity other than the TARGET ENTITY: a parent, subsidiary or affiliate)

scoring_rule: Unit = KYC fact, by group: registration 40% (7 fields), officers and owners 20% (capped at 5), screening findings 40% (critical 6, useful 2, minor 0.5). A false hit (wrong entity, or an event that did not happen) weighs 3x in accuracy; a wrong date or figure on a real finding counts 1x.

name: Deal sourcing and market mapping
instructions:
You build a list of private companies that fit the investment thesis in the input.

- Return ALL qualifying companies you can verify, however few. Never relax a criterion to reach a number.
- For each: name, domain, hq (city, state/country), founded_year, employee estimate with source, ownership
  (founder-owned | family-owned | PE-backed by <firm> | VC-backed), and evidence for each thesis criterion with source_url.
- Enrich each with headcount growth (two dated counts), last funding round, and one traction signal (customers,
  awards, revenue statements), each with source_url. Rank the list by fit and say why in rank_reason.
- Exclude companies already owned by a PE firm unless the thesis allows it. Check the company's news and the PE firm's
  portfolio page.
- Use industry association member lists, trade-show exhibitor lists, state registries, local business press and the
  companies' own sites.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.
inputs: Find founder-owned US commercial HVAC service companies in Texas with 50-300 employees and no institutional investors
Find founder- or family-owned US veterinary clinic groups with 5-30 locations
Find bootstrapped European vertical SaaS companies for logistics or freight with 50-200 employees
Find founder-owned US specialty chemical distributors with 50-250 employees and no private equity owner
Find family-owned German machine-tool manufacturers (Mittelstand) with 100-500 employees

unit.name: company
unit.definition: One unit per company the output returns as fitting the thesis: "<Company> (<domain>) fits the thesis". Evidence, enrichment fields and rank are NOT separate units.
unit.verify_rule: true only if the company really meets EVERY thesis criterion, including ownership; false if any criterion fails.

scoring_rule: Unit = company. Each thesis criterion is checked pass / fail / unknown. Qualifies if no criterion fails and the sector criterion passes. A company that passes everything except an unprovable ownership criterion counts half (partial) in coverage and accuracy.

name: Hedge-fund company research
instructions:
You write a research brief on ONE public company for a hedge-fund analyst deciding today.

Sections (each a list of short claims, every claim with a source_url and a date):
- catalysts: dated upcoming events that could move the stock in the next 6 months (earnings, product launches, court
  or regulatory decisions, debt maturities, index changes, lock-up expiries).
- results_vs_guidance: the latest reported quarter against the company's own guidance and consensus; the current guidance.
- event_driven: M&A, activists, spin-offs, buybacks, tender offers, strategic reviews.
- credit_signals: debt maturities, rating actions, covenants, liquidity, refinancing.
- alternative_signals: hiring and layoffs, pricing changes, contracts won or lost, trade-press and channel checks.
- insider_and_ownership: insider buying and selling (Form 4), 13D/13G filings, notable fund position changes.
- risks: what could break the thesis, each backed by a cited fact.
- research_view: 2-3 sentences on what matters most right now.

Read the rest of the web, not just headlines: filings and exhibits, court dockets, regulator sites, job posts, trade press.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.

unit.name: research finding
unit.definition: One unit per distinct finding a fund analyst would use: each dated catalyst, each result-vs-guidance figure, each event-driven item, each credit signal, each alternative signal, each insider or ownership move, each cited risk. Restatements and generic description are not units.
unit.verify_rule: true if the finding is correct, about this company, with the right date and figures; an upcoming catalyst must really be scheduled.

scoring_rule: Unit = research finding (catalyst, result vs guidance, event-driven item, credit or alternative signal, insider move, risk), weighted for a fund analyst deciding today: critical 6, useful 2, minor 0.5; x1.5 when fresh. F1.

name: Answer a current question with sources
instructions:
You answer ONE current question for an AI assistant that will show your answer to its user.

- answer: 2-5 sentences that answer the question as of today, most recent information first.
- key_facts: each distinct fact the answer rests on, with source_url and date.
- passages: the exact source passages (short quotes) that support the answer, each with source_url, publisher and
  published_date. Prefer primary sources (the company's own release or transcript, the regulator, the filing).
- caveats: what is uncertain, disputed or may have changed.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.

What guidance did Nike give for the current quarter on its most recent earnings call, and how did the stock react?

scoring_rule: Unit = fact the answer states or rests on, weighted by whether it is needed to answer correctly: critical 6, useful 2, minor 0.5; x1.5 when fresh. F1.

name: Adverse media investigation
instructions:
You investigate adverse information about ONE company for a financial-crime analyst.

- entity: the legal name, headquarters country and the group it belongs to.
- events: every distinct adverse event that matches the request (bribery, corruption, fraud, sanctions, money
  laundering, market manipulation, enforcement actions, major litigation). For each: date, type, jurisdiction,
  status (alleged / investigated / charged / settled / convicted / acquitted / dismissed), parties (which group
  entity or person), amount if any, a one-sentence summary and source_url. Court records, regulator and prosecutor
  releases first, then reputable press.
- excluded_namesakes: companies or people with similar names that you excluded, and why.
- assessment: 2-3 sentences on the overall risk and what is still open.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.

unit.name: adverse event
unit.definition: One unit per distinct adverse event (one allegation, investigation, charge, settlement or conviction in one jurisdiction), plus one unit per excluded namesake. The same event reported twice is one unit.
unit.verify_rule: true only if the event really happened, concerns this company or its group, and the date and legal status are right; an event about a namesake or with the wrong status (e.g. 'convicted' when only charged) is false.

judge_tag.spec: "materiality": "critical|useful|minor" (for a financial-crime analyst; charges, settlements and convictions are critical), "fresh": true|false

scoring_rule: Unit = adverse event (one allegation, charge, settlement or conviction in one jurisdiction) or excluded namesake; a wrong legal status or a namesake event is false. Weighted critical 6, useful 2, minor 0.5; x1.5 when fresh. F1.

name: Investment thesis testing
instructions:
You test ONE investment thesis for a fundamental analyst.

- evidence_for: facts that support the thesis (company figures and guidance, industry data, contracts, capacity,
  pricing), each with source_url, date and "strength": strong / moderate / weak.
- evidence_against: facts that cut against it, same format.
- counterarguments: the strongest arguments against the thesis, each tied to cited facts above.
- key_uncertainties: what is unknown and what data would resolve it.
- what_would_change_the_view: specific, observable events.
- verdict: 2-3 sentences: supported, partly supported or not supported, and why.
General rules:
- Today's date is {today}. Prefer the most recent source; give as_of for every number.
- Stay on the exact entity given. Do not drift to a namesake, a subsidiary, a parent or a similarly named company.
- Only return a value you read on a page you opened. Otherwise return null and list the field in missing_fields.
- Cite the page each value came from in source_url.
